$keyComment: Transparent assets: Codex is told to use image_gen's real alpha; if it paints a backdrop instead, it must be this flat colour, which img.gd keys out automatically (auto-key only fires when the image has no real alpha). Override per asset with "key" when the subject contains that colour (e.g. the magenta lighter uses the default green; a plant would use "ff00ff").

kinds.scene: A full-frame environment layer. Paint it as a finished game background: every surface has material shading, the lighting is unified, nothing is a placeholder. Composition must leave the centre-bottom area (where a customer bust will stand in front of the counter) uncluttered enough that a character reads clearly against it.
kinds.portrait: A head-and-shoulders bust for dialogue, cut off cleanly at roughly the chest/upper-arm line as in Coffee Talk (the counter hides the rest). Facing the viewer, slight three-quarter allowed. Transparent background. Same pixel density and outline weight as the target-state reference so every cast member matches.
kinds.icon: A single tiny pixel icon drawn on a deliberately coarse grid: render it as a 16x16 (or the stated size) pixel-art icon scaled up to fill the canvas with big, crisp, uniform square pixels and no anti-aliasing, so it downsamples cleanly. Flat 3-5 colour palette, 1-px dark outline, readable silhouette.
kinds.prop: A single small object as a game sprite, transparent background, front/slightly-above view consistent with sitting on the counter, clean outline, Coffee Talk material shading.
kinds.concept: A full-frame concept painting of a COMPOSED screen — the target the whole game is judged against. Not a sprite: it is kept at native size under concept-art/generated/ and never snapped. It must be a finished frame: unified lighting, one pixel grid, every surface resolved. No UI chrome (dialogue box, HUD) — the engine draws that — and no text except signage named in the prompt.

assets.prompt: CONCEPT ART for the game's core screen — the Berlin-Späti version of the attached interaction reference (image 1): the SAME framing, pixel density, rendering quality and warmth, but the set is a Berlin late-night kiosk (Späti), not a café. Centred and facing the viewer, cut off by the counter at the hips: Lena, a broke Berlin art student in her early 20s — pale, freckled, reddish-auburn hair escaping a dark green beanie, a paint-flecked oversized denim jacket over a striped top, a silver hoop earring — holding an empty Mate-like bottle up near her shoulder, a proud, slightly evasive half-smile. The worn warm-brown wooden counter fills the bottom ~22% of the frame with an amber highlight along its front edge; on it: a ceramic coffee cup on a saucer at ~30% of the width, a phone lying flat at ~50%, a compact cash register at the far right, a plastic Pfand crate of empty green bottles at the far left. Behind her, the shop from the shopkeeper's side: at the left a tall wall of glowing drinks fridges (cyan-white interior light) with generic green beer bottles with plain labels and yellow-label Mate-like bottles; dark wood panelling with shelves of stand-in snacks and tobacco pouches; a hand-painted warm neon 'SPÄTI' sign glowing high in the middle-left; a techno flyer and a small U-Bahn-style sign pinned to the wood; a football scarf (no real club) on a hook; a hanging plant; at the right the glass door onto a rainy, cold-blue Berlin street with a distant magenta neon and wet reflections. Three warm pendant lamps across the top pooling amber light; the middle behind Lena's head is calmer and darker so she reads. Mood: cozy, bittersweet, deep night. NO dialogue box, NO HUD, NO text anywhere except the SPÄTI sign.  This image becomes the target the whole game is judged against — make it the frame a Coffee Talk fan would accept as a sibling game set in Berlin. TRUE PIXEL ART, NOT A SMOOTH ILLUSTRATION: one locked logical grid of about 480 art pixels across the frame's width (≈ 4 screen pixels per art pixel at 1080p) — every contour is a stepped 1-px line on that grid, every material is 4–6 flat shade clusters, hair is grouped into a few large locks, eyelashes/lips/freckles are short stepped clusters, denim is clean midtone + broad shadow planes with a few separated paint clusters, bottle labels are simple blocks; no hairline strokes, no granular noise, no gradients, no anti-aliasing. CROP-SAFETY: the canvas is 3:2 but the game frame is 16:9 — treat the top ~12% and bottom ~12% as expendable margin and compose everything for the middle 16:9 band: within that band Lena's beanie top sits at ~10–12% of the height and the counter's top edge at ~77–78%; keep the Pfand crate and register small so the central counter stays a broad readable band; darken and simplify the street outside and the distant facade so Lena is the brightest focus after the fridges. Lena occupies about one third of the frame's width; the counter's rear edge sits at ~78% of the playable band (not lower); both forearms rest on the counter; shelving stays visible around her shoulders. Materials are calm: the counter is 4–5 wood tones with one clean warm highlight band, wall grain is simplified, the jacket's wear is a few broad patches, bottle reflections are single economical clusters.

assets.prompt:
TRUE PIXEL ART, NOT A SMOOTH ILLUSTRATION. Draw this as if a pixel artist placed every pixel on ONE locked grid at about 480x270 art pixels: chunky uniform square pixels, hard nearest-neighbour edges everywhere, 4-6 flat tones per material with stepped cluster shading, ordered dithering only for soft light falloff, clean 1-px dark outlines on every fixture. NO airbrushed glows, NO gaussian blur, NO anti-aliased or feathered edges, NO photographic glass reflections or sub-pixel glints, NO fine painterly noise, NO gradients. Every bottle, leaf and raindrop must be a deliberate cluster of a few pixels, not a rendered object.

SUBJECT: the interior of a Berlin Späti at night, seen from behind the counter (the shopkeeper's fixed side-on view: straight-on, at eye level, absolutely no isometric and no high angle), with NO people, NO counter and NO foreground objects — this is the flat back-wall layer that sits BEHIND a character bust.

FRAMING — the canvas is centre-cropped to 16:9 before use, so compose everything important inside the middle 16:9 band and treat the top ~15% and bottom ~15% of the canvas as expendable margin (ceiling darkness above, floor/plinth shadow below). Nothing readable may touch the top or bottom edge.

LEFT THIRD: a wall of drinks fridges seen through glass doors, cyan-white interior light, rows of generic bottles (green beer bottles with plain paper labels, yellow-label Mate-like bottles, water, cola-like). Keep the outer fridge casing dark and simple; simplify each shelf to a few repeated bottle silhouettes with low-contrast labels; reserve the brightest cyan-white for thin door-edge highlights only, so the fridges never out-shout the character.

MIDDLE THIRD: dark warm-brown vertical wood panelling, dressed but organised. The exact centre of the frame at head-and-chest height must stay CALM — plain panelling, no bright lamp, no poster, no glowing sign there. Around that calm pocket, to its left and right and above, hang flat kiosk fixtures in low contrast: a rack of abstract cigarette packs, small handwritten price cards, a row of key hooks, a little old radio, a taped-up notice, one narrow shelf of stand-in snacks and tobacco pouches. The hand-painted warm neon 'SPÄTI' sign glows HIGH in the LEFT of this middle band, sitting fully inside the 16:9 band with dark wood all around it and both umlaut dots drawn as two bright square pixel clusters so the word reads instantly.

RIGHT THIRD: the glass door and window onto the street — cold blue rainy Berlin night outside, wet pavement reflections in stepped bands, a distant magenta neon glow across the street, a bicycle silhouette, a small U-Bahn-style corner sign, a layered techno flyer and a few stickers taped to the inside of the glass (abstract shapes only, no readable text, no real logos), a hanging plant and a green-and-white football scarf (no real club) on a hook.

LIGHTING: two warm amber pendant lamps hang complete (whole shade visible, breathing room above) near the far left and far right; each pools a broad amber light shape with stepped cluster boundaries down its side of the room, leaving the middle dimmer. Warm highlight bands along shelf fronts and wood seams; a restrained cold blue rim on the edges facing the window. Compress the dark browns into two or three clear shadow families, not many near-blacks.

Dense but readable "wall of cozy stuff" like the Coffee Talk café, re-skinned as a Berlin kiosk; unified night lighting, warm amber interior against the cold blue window.

GLOW DISCIPLINE: every light source (both pendant lamps, the SPÄTI neon, the fridge interiors, the wet-street reflections) is built from 4-6 stepped concentric colour bands with deliberate cluster shapes and sparse ordered dithering at the transitions — no blurred outer halo, no continuous bloom, no isolated sub-grid speckles.

CHARACTER READ: a 150x230 bust will stand dead centre. Keep a low-contrast halo of at least 10 art pixels around where its head and shoulders will be: move hooks, notices and bright packets outward to the left and right of that pocket, darken the shelf segments and merchandise immediately behind it by one value step, and let no high-contrast shelf edge cut through it. The fridge interiors must be one value step darker than the central lamp pool and tinted pale cyan rather than white, so the warm centre stays the brightest area of the frame.

assets.prompt:
TRUE PIXEL ART, NOT A SMOOTH ILLUSTRATION AND NOT A PHOTOGRAPHIC TEXTURE. Draw this as if a pixel artist placed every pixel by hand on ONE locked grid of about 480x270 art pixels and the result were enlarged with nearest-neighbour: every art pixel is a solid uniform square block about 3x3 canvas pixels across, every edge hard and stepped, every diagonal a visible staircase. Nothing may be thinner than one of those blocks. Each material gets 4-6 FLAT tones in deliberately shaped clusters, sparse ordered dithering only at light falloff, and a clean 1-block dark outline. ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: anti-aliasing, blur, soft gradients, airbrushed glow, mottled or cloudy variation, photographic wood grain, random speckles and scratches, tiny half-pixel highlights, noise of any kind.

SUBJECT: the foreground counter band of a Berlin Spaeti seen from the shopkeeper's side, drawn as ONE wide horizontal strip that spans the FULL width of the canvas, edge to edge, and occupies only the BOTTOM 35% of the canvas. Straight-on eye-level view from just above the counter top, so a shallow band of the wooden surface is visible and the counter's front edge is perfectly horizontal and runs the whole width.

WOOD: a worn warm-brown wooden counter top and a darker plank front face below it. Build each of them from exactly four steps - a dark base, one midtone, one warm light tone and a few short horizontal grain marks, each grain mark a single straight block-wide dash. Plank seams are crisp 1-block dark lines aligned to the grid. No cloudy blotches, no continuous gradient along the top, no photographic figure in the wood.

LIGHT: an amber lamp pool falls across the middle of the counter top, built from 3-4 clearly stepped amber shapes with hard cluster boundaries (never one broad smooth glow), plus a narrow 1-2 block warm highlight band running along the front lip of the counter. Add a restrained COOL BLUE rim along the night-facing top edges of the props so their silhouettes stay readable. Raise the darkest values: keep near-black for outlines and creases only, never for whole shadow areas - the crate, the lower front face and the shadowed side of the register must still show a readable dark midtone.

OBJECTS RESTING ON THE COUNTER, left to right, each a compact well-outlined pixel prop with 4-5 tones: a low plastic Pfand crate of stubby empty green bottles at the FAR LEFT (dark gaps between the bottle necks, no vertical colour noise); a chipped mismatched ceramic mug LEFT OF CENTRE (no delicate porcelain saucer - a modest everyday mug, with a small bottle opener lying beside it); a mobile phone lying flat face-up NEAR THE CENTRE, its screen a dark slab with a 1-block pale cyan rim so it does not disappear into the wood; a small paper Pfand receipt with abstract tally marks; and a compact cash register at the FAR RIGHT with a blank unlit display panel (no glyphs, no digits, no text of any kind).

BERLIN LAYER: taped to the front face of the counter, flat and readable and entirely brand-free - one small angular techno-flyer fragment in magenta and black, one green-and-white football-colour sticker, and one small abstract BVG-style transit sticker in yellow. Abstract shapes only, no readable lettering. A few muted magenta and cyan reflected flecks on the phone rim, the mug glaze and the register's metal edges, while the dominant colour stays amber wood.

KEEP EVERY OBJECT LOW-PROFILE: nothing may rise more than about one third of the strip height above the counter top, and nothing at all may be drawn in the top half of the canvas. Do not draw any dark oval smudge, stain or hole on the counter surface.

BACKGROUND: the entire upper 65% of the canvas, everything above the counter and its objects, is empty background - transparent (real alpha), or one flat unshaded key colour if alpha is unavailable. Every edge where the counter or an object meets that background must be a hard, un-antialiased pixel edge with no glow, no soft fade and no coloured halo. No wall, no shelves, no people, no floor, no stools, no shadow cast onto the background.

Nothing - no outline, highlight, rain streak, shelf edge, window bar or cobble seam - may be thinner than one of those blocks. Shade every material with 4-6 flat tones in deliberately shaped clusters, use ordered dithering only where light falls off, and put a clean 1-block dark outline around every object. ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: anti-aliasing, blur, resampling softness, airbrush glow, bloom halos, smooth gradients, speckle, grain, film texture, photographic reflections, any sub-pixel detail.

LIGHT AS STEPPED CLUSTERS, NEVER GLOW: every light source (the sign, the window light, the doorway, the interior lamps, the puddle reflections) is a crisp emissive core surrounded by 2-3 hard-edged bands of progressively darker colour, each band a clearly shaped cluster with a stepped boundary. No feathered halo may bleed across a surface, no continuous bloom, no soft light spill on the facade.

KEEP IT SIMPLE ENOUGH TO READ AT 480x270: few big shapes, a handful of hero props, generous dark masses, clear dark gaps between groups of objects. No crowd of tiny posters, no micro-detail, no busy foliage. Brick, stucco and asphalt are FLAT tone blocks with a few deliberately placed darker blocks - never a texture.

SUBJECT: title-screen key art - the exterior of a small Berlin Spaeti (corner kiosk) on a rainy night, seen straight on from across the street.

FRAMING / CROP SAFETY: this canvas is centre-cropped to 16:9 and then downscaled 3.2x onto the 480x270 grid. Compose everything important inside the middle 16:9 band; treat the top ~8% and the bottom ~8% of the canvas as expendable margin. Nothing readable may touch the top or bottom edge and no large object may be cropped at the left or right edge.

COMPOSITION: push the whole storefront LOW. The shopfront occupies the lower two thirds of the frame; a wide, calm, DARK band of Berlin Altbau facade and rainy blue-black night sky fills the upper third, where the game logo will be overlaid. That upper band is deliberately low-contrast and almost empty: plain dark stucco and brick, at most two small dim windows far left and far right, nothing bright and no sign in the middle of it. The hand-painted SPAETI fascia sits LOW, directly above the shop window at roughly 60% of the frame height, small and wide, and it is DIM - a dull warm red-orange lit from within, no brighter than the shop windows, with NO tube bloom and no light spilling onto the wall above it - so a logo placed above will not have to fight it.

CONTENT: a lit shop window on each side of a central glass door, warm amber light spilling onto wet cobblestones. Inside each window, ONE clearly drawn drinks fridge: crisp dark frame, visible shelf edges and a door handle, and 2-3 rows of large, well-separated generic bottle silhouettes (green beer bottles, yellow-label Mate-like bottles) in 2-3 flat tones with dark gaps between the groups - readable props, never vertical colour noise, never a stripe pattern. A red plastic crate of empty bottles beside the door. A restrained Berlin layer, all flat readable pixel shapes and all brand-free: two club-flyer stickers and a small fictional transit-map fragment taped inside the glass, a green-and-white football-colour scarf decal, a small dark notice board by the door, a Pfand-return sign as an abstract bottle-and-arrow glyph. Rain as sparse straight light streaks exactly 1 block wide, all parallel, aligned to the grid, only over the dark areas. The wet pavement reflects the shop in SHORT horizontal pixel clusters aligned with the paving seams - the surrounding stone stays dark and flat, and the strongest warm reflection forms a narrow path from the bottom edge up to the doorway. Magenta and cyan reflected accents are small, hard-edged and few. No real brands, no logos, no readable lettering anywhere except the single word on the sign.

THE PROTAGONIST - draw him as a deliberately designed sprite, not a painted figure. A lone young man stands on the pavement facing the door, seen from behind at three-quarter with a sliver of his cheek and nose visible, one hand holding a set of keys. He is about one third of the image height (roughly 90 art pixels tall on the 480x270 grid), centred slightly LEFT of the door so his silhouette sits against the bright doorway. Build him from a few large flat clusters with a solid near-black outline all the way round: (a) HAIR - messy wavy mid-brown, drawn as 4-6 chunky tufts with a lighter brown top plane, no strands; (b) a BRIGHT RED hoodie whose hood is bunched as a clear red mass at the back of his neck, reading unmistakably red against the jacket; (c) an open jacket with warm BROWN torso panels and NEAR-BLACK shoulders and upper sleeves, the border between them a crisp straight cluster edge, and ONE clean red band across each sleeve just above the elbow; (d) dark blue jeans in two tones; (e) dark sneakers with a red accent block. Light him with a warm amber rim exactly 1-2 blocks wide down his back, shoulder and hair from the doorway, and leave his front in flat shadow - two values only, no modelling. His silhouette must stay unbroken and readable against the lit doorway.

The protagonist 'You' (Onkel Cem's nephew) - he must read as EXACTLY the man in the target-state reference image, same person, same age, same face, same hair, same clothes. FACE (the judge docked this hardest - the face came out older and more anime): a SHORT, WIDE lower face with a soft rounded chin and a gentle jawline, not a long pointed anime jaw; boyish mid-20s; features set close together in the middle of the face; SMALL calm brown eyes with one white highlight pixel each and thin low-contrast brows, never large glossy anime eyes or heavy dark brows; a small nose; a small closed level mouth; the ear small and tucked, barely protruding; pale muted peach skin, only the faintest hint of stubble. HAIR: a LOW, compact crown of short tousled dark-brown curls built from a few overlapping rounded clusters that hug the skull - no tall spiky silhouette, no long isolated flyaway spikes, no strand-by-strand painting; colour is muted olive-dark-brown with only a restrained warm highlight cluster on the lit side - NEVER orange, NEVER reddish, never ginger; the ears stay exposed. CLOTHES: a dusty crimson (not bright, not orange) hoodie with visible drawstrings and a small plain light chest patch (a blank shape - never a logo, swoosh, brand mark or lettering), worn under the layered jacket exactly as in the reference: taupe-brown front chest panels, charcoal-black shoulder yoke and sleeves, a compact dark collar, one narrow clean red band across each upper sleeve, seams where the reference puts them. Normal slim shoulders - do NOT broaden them. EXPRESSION: neutral, relaxed brows, eyes open, quietly tired and uncertain, not stern. FRAMING: head-and-shoulders bust, centred, facing the viewer, slightly below eye level, cut cleanly across the mid-torso at chest height with both shoulders resolving evenly inside the canvas; hands, forearms and any stray arm wedge are out of frame; leave clear space above the crown so no hair tuft touches the top edge. LIGHT: soft and mostly even; a narrow warm amber rim on the upper left only, a faint cool-blue edge on the right, cool charcoal shadows. Nothing saturated or orange. RENDERING DISCIPLINE (this is what failed before): draw it as a TRUE PIXEL-ART SPRITE on ONE consistent pixel grid - imagine a 190x230 sprite blown up, every cluster a hard-edged block of one flat colour. About 4-6 flat tones per material and nothing more; large intentional clusters instead of tiny stair-stepped filigree; one clean 1-pixel dark contour around the figure and the major shapes. NO quasi-anti-aliased transitions, NO soft gradients, NO airbrushing, NO speckled colour noise, NO isolated stray pixels, NO painterly illustration look. Simple clean cel-shaded Coffee Talk portrait, closer to a friendly visual-novel bust than to a realistic painting. BACKGROUND: the PNG must have a REAL alpha channel around the bust - do NOT paint a grey-and-white checkerboard pattern to fake transparency, that is a hard rejection; if image_gen cannot give you alpha, fill the whole background with ONE flat solid #00ff00 instead. No text, no watermark, no border, no frame, no second panel.
